hookSwap.$comment: The placeValue4Digit hook asserted something a Sri Lankan child knows is false. Books here cost 3-digit prices, so 'book prices are four-digit numbers' is wrong on the facts — and a hook that opens on something the child can see is untrue costs more than a weak hook does. A school bag genuinely runs to four digits. Round 2's logic fix is kept: what makes the number readable is knowing where its digits sit, not how many there are. Both sentences stay under 14 words.

softenToSoftCheck.$comment: Half the authored ASKs become SOFT_CHECKs. An ASK stops the lesson, opens the mic for a judged answer and runs an 8s/12s/10s silence ladder into FEEDBACK or RETEACH; a SOFT_CHECK opens the mic for 3s, warmly acknowledges any sound, and flows on unjudged. The script asked one judged question every 35s, so a 12-minute sitting carried ~21 of them. Every beat kept below is a real checkpoint; every beat here is a repeat of the checkpoint before it, or a question that answers itself, or one that cannot be judged at all. Beat TYPE and pauseType both change; the words are untouched.

neutralConfirmation.$comment: ROUND 4, THE SYSTEMIC ONE. The runtime already plays a praise or a miss clip based on what the child actually said (AUTHORED_LINES.feedbackCorrect / feedbackWrong, chosen by the planner). A scripted beat that ALSO congratulates therefore congratulates unconditionally — it plays word for word after a wrong answer, after a retry, and after silence that ended in Zara demonstrating the answer herself. Every beat that follows a question is now a NEUTRAL statement of the answer, which is true in all three cases. The praise did not go away; it moved to the only place that knows whether it is deserved.

authoringRule.$comment: ROUND 4, for every future lesson. Added to the author's prompt (scripts/author-script.ts) so this class of bug is not written again.
authoringRule.rule: The beat following any question is a neutral statement of the answer. Never write praise or a verdict into a scripted beat; the runtime supplies praise and miss lines based on the real answer.

validatorAudit.$comment: ROUND 4. What the two new rules found across all beats, and what was done about each.

noAssumedAnswer.action: NONE — all three were false positives, and the rule was narrowed instead. Each follows a SOFT_CHECK that ends on a rhetorical tag ('කූරු හතරේ පිළිවෙළ ඔයාට මතක හිටියා නේද?'), which is a confirmation rather than an invitation to produce a number; the number that follows is Zara choosing her own example, not assuming the child's. The rule now fires only on a question that actually asks the child to make something — 'ඔයා කැමති', or no expectedAnswer AND no rhetorical tag.

visualContinuity.$comment: ROUND 7 — the third native review: the script 'holds together conversationally'; what remained was the board. Two facts first. (1) At runtime a beat with board 'none' has ALWAYS inherited the previous board — stageBeatBoard returns nothing for it and the runtime only repaints on a staged board — so no beat below changed its runtime meaning. What changed is that 'none' is now DOCUMENTED as inherit, the review doc prints what is inherited instead of the word 'none', and blanking on purpose has its own word, {kind:'clear'}, which this script uses nowhere: both concept boundaries land on a title card, which replaces the board outright, and a clear before it would be the exact flash the new validator forbids. (2) No content_bank ExpansionExercise row contains 5421, so :96 stages a synthetic one.

storyboard.$comment: STORYBOARD ROUND. docs/storyboard/script-notes.md put the visual plan against every line; four lines carried more than two things to show in one sentence, one said 'let's look' at a board with nothing new on it, and two board intents fought the picture. The accepted notes, applied. Text changes re-key their clips by construction (a clip key is the hash of the words); no human take existed for any of them.

authored:placeValue4Digit:34.why: Found while applying B1. The bare abacus was staged as digits [0,0,0,0], and boardPatch caps beads at digits[rod] — so :39 and :40 landed NOTHING on the real board, and the old :41 full re-stage with animate was painting the finished abacus over that. Rods still start bare (startEmpty); the target is now the number being built, so each abacus_add lands its beads and the child watches 5 421 assemble rod by rod.
